items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: When the Pacific was going out then, that's when Bunny Dash started to come in there beating drum. See, that was the son of Clay Dash.

ctx.x: Clay Dash, yeah. Then, later, the son. When the Pacific was going out then, that's when Bunny Dash started to come in there beating drum. See, that was the son of Clay Dash. Yeah. He died in, uh, in Baton Rouge. He married and went to Baton Rouge.

About how big a band was that altogether? About how many cornets did they use? Yeah, three cornets. Three cornets. Three cornets. How many trombones? Two. Two. And they used alto horns those days. Alto, alto, biotone, clarinet, bass, snare drum. Two drums, yeah. Yeah, two drums, yeah. Um, I remember Manuel Moneta told us something, I believe, about a band the Southern Pacific had, too. Did they have some of the fellows that worked for them? Well, they- Have a band for the Southern Pacific? I didn't know whether-…
